Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class BelongsToMany<R extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.Relation<R,BelongsToMany<R>>
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.BelongsToMany<R>
Type Parameters:
R - the related model class
Direct Known Subclasses:
MorphToMany
public class BelongsToMany<R extends Model> extends Relation<R,BelongsToMany<R>>
A many-to-many relation through a pivot table, such as a user's roles through role_user: Laravel's BelongsToMany.

The relation joins the related table to the pivot table on the related key, and filters the pivot table on the parent's key. Each related row comes back with its pivot as the pivot relation (or the name set by as), built from the pivot_* columns the read selects. A related model linked to two parents is two instances, each with its own pivot.

These methods return the relation, so they chain in any order. The settings and conditions are withPivot, withTimestamps, as, using, withPivotValue, chaperone, withoutChaperone, the wherePivot family, orWherePivot, wherePivotIn, wherePivotBetween, wherePivotNull, orderByPivot and orderByPivotDesc. The readers are find, findMany, findOrFail, findOr, first, firstOrFail, firstOr, firstWhere, sole, chunk, chunkById, each, lazy, lazyById, cursor, paginate, simplePaginate and cursorPaginate, each in its builder form: they run on a copy of the relation's query, so the relation itself is unchanged by a read.

Relation.get() and getResults() run the lazy query. Relation.getQuery() returns the relation's own query with the join and the parent constraint but without the pivot aliases and without the pivot hydration: a read through it returns plain related models.

Subclassing is possible only from this package. The constructor and the hooks that choose the select step and the pivot instances are package-private, so a subclass in another package cannot be built or override them.

Not safe to share across threads, and single use: build a relation for each query, through the model's typed method or relation(name). Each read copies the query and creates its own hydrator, so a relation read twice sends the same SQL both times.

  • Method Details

    • getResults

      public ModelCollection<R> getResults()
      Returns the related models of the parent. A parent without a key value runs no query and gets an empty collection.
      Specified by:
      getResults in class Relation<R extends Model,BelongsToMany<R extends Model>>
      Returns:
      the related models in query order, never null

    • get

      public final ModelCollection<R> get(String... columns)
      Runs the lazy query with the given columns. The columns apply only when the relation's query selects nothing; a select the relation already has is kept and the columns are ignored.
      Parameters:
      columns - the related columns to select, or none for every related column; no null element
      Returns:
      the related models in query order, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if columns is null

    • newPivot

      public Pivot newPivot(Map<String,?> attributes, boolean exists)
      Creates the pivot of one row: the attributes moved out of the row, in the relation's pivot class when one was given and in the plain pivot class otherwise. The values recorded by withPivotValue are merged under the attributes, so an attribute given here wins.
      Parameters:
      attributes - the pivot columns with their prefix removed, never null
      exists - whether the row is in the database
      Returns:
      the new pivot, never null

    • save

      public final R save(R model, Map<String,?> pivotAttributes, boolean touch)
      Saves the related model and links it to the parent. A save vetoed by a hook leaves the model unsaved and unlinked; check Model.exists(). Touches run after the commit. A model bound to another connection than the parent is saved outside the link transaction.
      Parameters:
      model - the related model, never null
      pivotAttributes - the join-table attributes of the link, never null
      touch - whether to touch the owners after the link
      Returns:
      the same model
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if model or pivotAttributes is null

    • sync

      public SyncResult sync(Object ids)
      Makes the join table hold exactly the ids given: attaches the missing ones, updates the attributes of the present ones and detaches the rest. It reads every current link of the parent, as Laravel does. The read and the writes take no lock; a racing call on a unique index fails cleanly and rolls back, and the owner touches run after the commit.
      Parameters:
      ids - a value, a model, a collection or array of either, or a map from id to its pivot attributes
      Returns:
      the attached, detached and updated keys, each cast to the related key type
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if ids is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if an element is null or a model has no related key

    • sync

      public SyncResult sync(Object ids, boolean detaching)
      Attaches the missing ids and updates the present ones, and detaches the others only when asked. It reads every current link of the parent, as Laravel does. The read and the writes take no lock; a racing call on a unique index fails cleanly and rolls back, and the owner touches run after the commit.
      Parameters:
      ids - a value, a model, a collection or array of either, or a map from id to its pivot attributes
      detaching - whether current keys absent from ids are detached
      Returns:
      the attached, detached and updated keys, each cast to the related key type
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if ids is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if an element is null or a model has no related key

    • withPivot

      public BelongsToMany<R> withPivot(String... columns)
      Adds extra pivot columns to read, after the ones already added. A column already present is not added again, and an empty argument list changes nothing.

      The values come back on each related model as attributes that are not dirty. A later discardChanges() on the related model restores them.

      A column that contains a dot is refused, because each column is read under an alias built from its name. Every column is checked before any is added, so a refused call changes nothing.

      Parameters:
      columns - the pivot columns, never null, no null element
      Returns:
      this relation
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if columns or one of its elements is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if a column contains a dot; nothing is added

      Returns:
